evals.prompt: I want to add Duende User Management to my existing IdentityServer project. I'd like passwordless login via email OTP, using SQLite for storage. Show me the full setup including packages needed and Program.cs changes.
evals.expected_output: Complete setup with NuGet packages (Duende.UserManagement.IdentityServer8, Duende.Storage.Sqlite), AddStorage(storage => storage.AddSqlite(...)) on the IdentityServer builder, AddUserManagement() with OTP dispatcher, and IStorageInstanceSchema.MigrateAsync() via IStorageInstanceSchemaFactory.
assertions: Adds Duende.UserManagement.IdentityServer8 NuGet package
Adds Duende.Storage.Sqlite NuGet package (or references it)
Calls AddUserManagement() on the IdentityServer builder with a configuration lambda
Selects the SQLite provider with AddStorage(storage => storage.AddSqlite(...)) on the IdentityServer builder (not inside the AddUserManagement lambda)
Creates the database schema with IStorageInstanceSchema.MigrateAsync() resolved from IStorageInstanceSchemaFactory.GetStorageInstanceSchema(...)

evals.prompt: I need to configure an OTP email dispatcher for production using SMTP. Show me how to set it up with Duende User Management.
evals.expected_output: Configuration using options.Authentication(auth => auth.UseSmtpOtpDispatcher(...)) inside AddUserManagement with SmtpOtpDispatcherOptions (Host, Port, EnableSsl, required FromEmail and FromName).
assertions: Uses options.Authentication(auth => auth.UseSmtpOtpDispatcher(...)) inside the AddUserManagement options lambda
Configures SMTP host and port
Sets the required FromEmail and FromName options (not invented Username/Password/FromAddress)
Does NOT use ConsoleOtpDispatcher for production (or warns against it)

evals.prompt: I'm setting up User Management with PostgreSQL for production. Show me the storage configuration and explain if I need to run database migrations.
evals.expected_output: Configuration using AddStorage(storage => storage.AddPostgreSql()) with an NpgsqlDataSource registered in DI, explanation that storage is document-based so no EF migrations are needed, and IStorageInstanceSchema.MigrateAsync() (ideally as a deployment step in production) to create the schema.
assertions: Registers an NpgsqlDataSource singleton from the connection string and selects PostgreSQL with AddStorage(storage => storage.AddPostgreSql())
Adds Duende.Storage.PostgreSql package (or references it)
Explains that no EF Core migrations are needed (document-based storage) but the common storage schema must still be created
Shows IStorageInstanceSchema.MigrateAsync() resolved via IStorageInstanceSchemaFactory, and notes that in production it should run as a controlled deployment step rather than app startup

evals.prompt: We have an existing app using ASP.NET Identity for user management. We want to migrate to Duende User Management. How do we import existing users without them losing access?
evals.expected_output: A hosted service reads the source ASP.NET Identity database (e.g. IdentityDbContext), maps users to UserImportRecord (SubjectId, ProfileAttributes, AuthenticatorImport.Password = PasswordImport(HashedPasswordData)) and calls IUserImporter.ImportAsync in batches. A custom IPasswordHashAlgorithm registered via auth.AddPasswordHashAlgorithm<T>() verifies the preserved hash, and passwords are re-hashed on first login. Re-runs skip existing users unless an IUserImportConflictResolver is registered.
assertions: Reads the source ASP.NET Identity DB and calls IUserImporter.ImportAsync with UserImportRecord(s) (does not use a non-existent AddAspNetIdentityMigration option)
Stores existing hashes via PasswordImport(HashedPasswordData) and registers a custom IPasswordHashAlgorithm (AddPasswordHashAlgorithm<T>) to verify them, with re-hash on first successful login
Mentions re-runs skip existing users by default, and an IUserImportConflictResolver can overwrite
Mentions that after migration users can enroll in passwordless methods

evals.prompt: How do I integrate Duende User Management with IdentityServer so that user claims are available in tokens? I need the user's email and custom profile attributes to appear in ID tokens. Show the complete IdentityServer integration in Program.cs, including how IdentityServer is pointed at the login and logout pages.
evals.expected_output: Explanation that AddUserManagement() automatically registers IProfileService, claims are mapped from user profile attributes based on requested scopes (openid, profile, email), and custom attributes can be exposed through custom identity resources.
assertions: Explains that AddUserManagement() automatically registers IProfileService
Mentions that claims mapping is based on requested scopes (openid → sub, email → email)
Notes that custom user attributes can be exposed via custom identity resources
Sets LoginUrl and LogoutUrl in IdentityServer options to point to account pages

evals.prompt: What authentication methods does Duende User Management support? I want to offer passkeys as the primary method with TOTP as fallback.
evals.expected_output: List of supported methods (OTP, TOTP, passkeys/WebAuthn, passwords, external, recovery codes), explanation that passkeys use WebAuthn/FIDO2, TOTP uses RFC 6238 authenticator apps, and both can coexist.
assertions: Lists passkeys/WebAuthn/FIDO2 as a supported authentication method
Lists TOTP (authenticator apps) as a supported method
Mentions that multiple authentication methods can coexist for the same user
Notes that OTP (email/SMS) is the default passwordless flow

evals.prompt: I'm getting errors when setting up User Management. I put AddSqliteStore(...) inside the AddUserManagement lambda, and the database is never created. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Explanation that storage is selected with AddStorage(storage => storage.AddSqlite(...)) on the IdentityServer builder (AddUserManagement only maps its data to a storage instance) and the schema must be created with IStorageInstanceSchema.MigrateAsync().
assertions: Identifies that the storage provider is selected with AddStorage(...) on the IdentityServer builder, not inside the AddUserManagement lambda
Shows the correct pattern: .AddStorage(storage => storage.AddSqlite(options => options.ConnectionString = ...)).AddUserManagement(...)
Mentions the schema must be created/migrated with IStorageInstanceSchema.MigrateAsync()
Does NOT suggest using EF Core migrations as a fix

evals.prompt: My IdentityServer already uses Duende Storage (AddStorage + AddConfigurationStorage + AddOperationalStorage). I'm adding User Management but want its data in a separate PostgreSQL database to isolate write load. How do I wire this up and migrate it?
evals.expected_output: Create a StorageInstanceId, register a second storage instance with AddStorage(instanceId, ...) and map User Management with AddUserManagement(instanceId, ...); migrate each instance via IStorageInstanceSchemaFactory.
assertions: Creates a StorageInstanceId (e.g. StorageInstanceId.Create("user-management"))
Registers the second database with AddStorage(storageInstanceId, storage => storage.AddPostgreSql(...))
Maps User Management to it with AddUserManagement(storageInstanceId, ...)
Migrates the named instance explicitly using IStorageInstanceSchemaFactory.GetStorageInstanceSchema(storageInstanceId, ct).MigrateAsync
Does NOT call AddStorage twice for the default instance (selecting a second provider for the same instance throws InvalidOperationException)

evals.prompt: I want to add a 'department' attribute to the built-in Duende User Management user profile and keep email/name attributes. Then later I want admins to edit the schema at runtime. Show me both approaches.
evals.expected_output: BuiltInSchemas.UserProfile.Extend(department) registered with AddInMemoryDataExtensionSchemas; for runtime editing, AddDynamicSchemas() with ISchemaAdmin get-modify-UpdateAsync using version; note that in-memory schemas are not used with AddDynamicSchemas.
assertions: Defines an AttributeDefinition with AttributeCode.Create("department") and a ScalarAttributeType string
Uses BuiltInSchemas.UserProfile.Extend(...) and registers the result with AddInMemoryDataExtensionSchemas([...])
Notes Extend throws InvalidOperationException if the attribute code already exists (e.g. email, name)
Shows AddDynamicSchemas() and ISchemaAdmin get-modify-UpdateAsync using the returned Version for optimistic concurrency
Warns that with AddDynamicSchemas() the in-memory schemas (including the built-in profile) are not used or seeded, so the schema must be created in the database
